evals.prompt: /storyboard Here's my explainer script (script.md). Can you break it into a storyboard I can review?
evals.expected_output: Should divide the script into visual beats (not a fixed count), generate an opaque 16:9 storyboard image per graphic beat, write a manifest following the documented schema with stable beat IDs, and build a standalone local HTML preview showing each beat's image, script range/transcript excerpt, visual objective, and review status. Should stop for review rather than building React/Remotion scenes.
assertions: Stays in storyboard mode, does not create Remotion/React scene files
Generates opaque-background images for graphic beats, not transparent
Writes a manifest with stable beat IDs matching references/preview-schema.md
Produces a standalone local HTML preview usable without a dev server

evals.prompt: $storyboard I approved beats 1-4 in the preview, now build the Remotion scenes for them.
evals.expected_output: Should enter scene/build mode only for the approved beats, create HTML/React/TypeScript scenes that reproduce each approved storyboard image, animate with useCurrentFrame()/spring()/interpolate() (not CSS transitions), keep full-background graphics opaque, render a frame and compare it against the approved storyboard image before calling a scene done, and update the implementation preview with links to each scene/source image/rendered frame.
assertions: Only builds the approved beats, not unapproved ones
Uses useCurrentFrame()/spring()/interpolate() rather than CSS transitions or Tailwind animation classes
Renders and compares a frame against the approved storyboard image before declaring a scene complete
Updates the implementation preview with scene/source/render links

evals.prompt: $storyboard Scenes are built for my talking-head video. Beat 3 is a lower-third callout over me talking, and beats 5 and 6 are full-screen graphics with about half a second of me on camera between them. Check it all over before I render.
evals.expected_output: Should render frames sampled across each beat (not just the first frame) composited over the source video, confirm the beat 3 callout never overlaps the speaker's face and reposition or shrink it if it does, and flag the ~0.5s return to footage between beats 5 and 6 as a glitch — merging the two full-screen graphics into one continuous run rather than cutting back to the speaker for under a second.
assertions: Renders and inspects composited frames rather than reviewing from code
Samples frames across the whole overlay beat, not only its first frame
Moves or resizes the callout if it overlaps the face, instead of just lowering opacity
Merges beats 5 and 6 into one continuous graphic run because the footage gap is under ~1s
